caption: We didn't realise until we did this exercise that we're both quietly sending money home every month. Do you and your partner actually know each other's full numbers?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R44 000
household income
Living in Paarl
slides.body:
Him 28, her 27
Married, no kids yet
Jobs: Viticulture technician & preschool teacher
Combined net: R44 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.includes: 2 bed starter home outside Paarl, rates included
slides.body: We bought before prices in the winelands went mad. Glad we didn't wait another year.

slides.title: Car instalments
slides.includes: His bakkie for the farm roads, her Fiesta
slides.body: Two cars because the farm and the school run in opposite directions every morning.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers big shop, Spar top-ups, his padkos for the farm
slides.body: We planned meals properly for about a month. We've since given up and just shop twice a week.

slides.title: Takeaways & date night
slides.includes: Friday dinner out, the odd delivery
slides.body: We told each other it was maybe R900. It's R1 800. Neither of us is surprised.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Both of us on the farm's group scheme
slides.body: Cheaper through his employer than either of us could get alone.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, phone & fibre, funeral policies x2, stokvel, black tax to both families, savings, gym
slides.body: Eighteen thousand seven hundred rand of things we'd only ever budgeted for separately before this.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R44 000 between us. On paper that's comfortable. After the bond and two cars, it doesn't feel like it some months.

slides.title: We stopped assuming our numbers matched
slides.body:
We put both our statements into Beyond Horizon and split the budget by category for the first time.

Neither of us knew the other was still sending money home until we saw it on one screen.

No bank login needed.
